'''Michael Polanyi''' ({{lang-hu|Polányi Mihály}}; March 11, 1891 – February 22, 1976) was a Hungarian-British polymath who made foundational theoretical contributions to physical chemistry, economics, and philosophy. Following a distinguished career in chemical dynamics, X-ray diffraction, and crystal dislocation theory at the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute in Berlin and the [[University of Manchester]], he turned to the philosophy of science and epistemology, developing an account of [[tacit knowledge]], [[emergence]], and hierarchical boundary conditions.

Polanyi is the author of ''Personal Knowledge: Towards a Post-Critical Philosophy'' (1958), ''The Tacit Dimension'' (1966), and the 1968 ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' article "Life's Irreducible Structure".<ref name="Science1968">{{cite journal |last=Polanyi |first=Michael |year=1968 |title=Life's Irreducible Structure |journal=Science |volume=160 |issue=3834 |pages=1308–1312 |doi=10.1126/science.160.3834.1308}}</ref> His philosophical work argues that all explicit knowing relies upon a subsidiary, embodied root of tacit knowing ("we can know more than we can tell"), and that living and engineered systems are organized through a hierarchy of boundary conditions in which higher-level principles harness lower-level physical and chemical laws without violating them.

His account of hierarchical boundary conditions and dual control has been examined alongside contemporary dynamical systems theory and [[Alicia Juarrero]]'s philosophy of ''causality as constraint''.<ref name="Takaki">{{cite journal |last=Takaki |first=K. |title=Juarrero, Polanyi, and Complexity |journal=Tradition & Discovery |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=5–15 |url=https://polanyisociety.org/TAD%20WEB%20ARCHIVE/TAD40-1/TAD40-1-fnl-pg5-15-pdf.pdf}}</ref>

== Philosophical work ==

=== Tacit knowing and the from–to structure ===

In ''Personal Knowledge'' (1958) and ''The Tacit Dimension'' (1966), Polanyi formulates the principle that human knowledge is never exhaustively formalizable: "we can know more than we can tell."<ref name="Tacit1966">{{cite book |last=Polanyi |first=Michael |title=The Tacit Dimension |publisher=Doubleday |year=1966}}</ref>

Polanyi analyzes skillful action and perception through a triad of **subsidiary awareness**, **focal awareness**, and the **knower** who integrates them. When a person uses a probe or cane to explore a dark cavern, the impacts on the palm and fingers are experienced subsidiarily; they are integrated into a focal awareness of the geometry at the tip of the probe. The structure of tacit knowing is therefore directional (**from** subsidiary particulars **to** a coherent focal whole). Attempting to switch focal attention exclusively to the subsidiary particulars dissolves the coherent meaning of the performance until re-integrated.

=== Dual control and boundary conditions ("Life's Irreducible Structure", 1968) ===

In "Life's Irreducible Structure" (1968), Polanyi examines how machines, texts, and biological organisms relate to the laws of physics and chemistry.<ref name="Science1968"/>

A physical or chemical law describes how a system evolves given a set of initial and boundary conditions, yet the laws of physics leave open a wide range of boundary conditions. In a machine—such as a clock, an oscilloscope, or a digital processor—the materials obey the laws of physics and chemistry at every instant, while the **shape and arrangement** of the parts act as fixed boundary conditions that channel physical forces toward an operational purpose.

Polanyi calls this **dual control**:
* **Lower-level control**: the laws of physics and chemistry governing the substrate;
* **Higher-level control**: the boundary conditions (constraints, organizational geometry, or informational code) that harness those laws without altering them.

Because the laws of physics are indifferent to the boundary conditions that harness them, the specification of a machine, a linguistic utterance, or a genetic/epigenetic organization is **irreducible** to physics and chemistry alone, even though its failure modes (such as mechanical fracture or thermal drift) are governed by physical law.

=== Relation to Alicia Juarrero and publication projections ===

Scholarship in complexity studies—including K. Takaki's analysis in ''Tradition & Discovery''—links Polanyi's account of boundary conditions directly to [[Alicia Juarrero]]'s account of **enabling, constitutive, and governing constraints**.<ref name="Takaki"/> Where Polanyi modeled boundary conditions primarily through machines and informational hierarchies, Juarrero generalizes boundary conditions to **endogenous, self-organizing dynamical constraints** in far-from-equilibrium systems.

In information-theoretic governance (such as Flyxion's *The Publication Projection*, 2026), Polanyi's from–to structure and boundary-condition hierarchy explain why a sensor's **publication projection** $P(y \mid x)$ can preserve the focal public utility $U(P) \ge u_{\min}$ (the coherent higher-level event or acoustic envelope) while discarding the raw subsidiary substrate $X$ at the boundary.
